verdictInOneParagraph: The repair is real, measured, non-vacuous, self-auditing and strictly dominates its predecessor: I reproduced the five-shape table exactly, reproduced 216/216 invariance and the 44-of-216 predecessor control exactly, built my own eleven-document catch matrix and measured v6 at 11/11 in both plain and array-wrapped form, verified every declared exit code at process level, verified all four self-audit gates FIRE under injected mutation, and verified the harness control byte for byte. The law-18 half delivers in full: number(int), number(float), boolean true, boolean false and null each raise ATTRIBUTION-UNCOMPARED-TYPE at a coordinate, at every container depth, and no scalar type is silently dropped. The blocker is not the repair; it is the CLAIM. The file, and freeze 4.4's head block, publish the class as CLOSED and assert that 'nesting cannot change a verdict' and that 'a shape nobody has thought of is handled by construction'. A three-line document falsifies both, with the exact terminal symptom of the blocker this successor exists to close: zero findings, zero mentions, artifact named nowhere, exit 0. The derivation ('an array does not name its members, an object does') is SOUND and is implemented correctly in the walk; the assumption is not removed, it is RELOCATED one function downstream into coordinate_qualifier, which consumes the correctly-accumulated qualifier list by taking only the INNERMOST coordinate-naming key and discarding every outer one. The walk appends; the resolver discards. And the container sweep offered as mechanical proof cannot see this by construction, because its wrapper keys are the neutral literals 'wrapper' and 'inner'. Run the instrument's OWN sweep with a wrapper key that names the packet's own date coordinate and it reports v6 losing a family in 24 of 90 pairs, six of them to total silence, including the vector labelled THE ESCAPE THIS SUCCESSOR CLOSES.

claim1_theDerivation.claimUnderTest: an ARRAY does not name its members, an OBJECT does - the walk appends a key descending into an object, nothing descending into an array; a leaf carries every object key on its path and is a coordinate if any qualifies. Containers become transparent, so a shape nobody has thought of is handled by construction.
claim1_theDerivation.questionAsked: Is that sound, or does it merely relocate the assumption?
claim1_theDerivation.answer: SOUND AS A RULE, RELOCATED AS AN IMPLEMENTATION. The rule is correct and qualified_leaves() implements it correctly: descending into an object appends the key, descending into an array appends nothing, and the leaf arrives carrying the ordered set of object keys on its path. I verified that directly. The assumption is not removed; it moves one function downstream. coordinate_qualifier() then CONSUMES that correctly-accumulated set by iterating reversed(qualifiers) and RETURNING ON THE FIRST MATCH - the innermost coordinate-naming key wins and every outer key is discarded. So the walk accumulates and the resolver throws the accumulation away. The predecessor assumed 'the key immediately above the scalar decides'. This successor assumes 'the innermost coordinate-naming key on the path decides'. Both are single-key assumptions. The new one is strictly harder to defeat with NEUTRAL wrapper keys and exactly as easy to defeat with a COORDINATE-NAMED one.

BLOCKER_B_PD6_01.title: THE COORDINATE-SHADOW ESCAPE. Interposing an object whose member key names the packet's own WHEN coordinate reassigns an authority leaf away from the WHO branch, and neither the comparison nor the type gate then names it. Total silence, artifact named nowhere, exit 0 - the exact terminal symptom of B-PD5-01, which this successor exists to close.

measuredAsRealBytesThroughASubprocess.plant: COORDINATE SHADOW through an array {signedOffBy:[{decidedOn:'product owner'}]}

BLOCKER_B_PD6_01.mechanism: coordinate_qualifier() iterates reversed(qualifiers) and returns on the first key that names a coordinate. For {decidedBy: {decidedOn: X}} the qualifier list is ('decidedBy','decidedOn'); reversed, 'decidedOn' matches coordinate_keys['when'] first and the function returns ('when','decidedOn'), discarding 'decidedBy' entirely. attribution_failures then takes the WHEN path, which compares only values that ARE calendar dates - and 'product owner' is not one. The WHO path is never entered because the coordinate is not 'who'. The type gate does not fire because emit_uncompared() is reached only when kind != 'string', and the forged authority IS a string. Three independent guards each decline, each for a locally correct reason, and the composition is silence.
BLOCKER_B_PD6_01.whyThisIsTheSAMECLASS: The class is not 'arrays'. The class is 'a container interposed between the naming key and the scalar destroys the comparison'. v5's interposition was an array. This is an object whose key happens to name a different coordinate. The head block's own words - 'a scalar reached through any number of arrays carries the key of the nearest enclosing OBJECT' - are true; what is false is the inference that carrying the key means the key is USED.
falsifiesThreePublishedSentences: file docstring, qualified_leaves: 'Containers become TRANSPARENT to the comparison, and nesting cannot change a verdict.' - MEASURED FALSE: flat gives 1 finding, nested gives 0.
freeze 4.4 head block: 'Containers become transparent rather than enumerated, so a shape nobody has thought of is handled by construction.' - MEASURED FALSE.

residual A14, verbatim: 'a scalar under an authority-shaped key keeps that key through arrays, and an object member key is APPENDED rather than replacing it. So a forger cannot escape by wrapping' - MEASURED FALSE. The key is appended to the qualifier LIST and then dropped by the RESOLVER.
BLOCKER_B_PD6_01.whyTheSWEEPCANNOTSEEIT: wrap_scalars() rewrites scalars into CONTAINER_SHAPES, whose object-valued members use the literal wrapper keys 'wrapper' and 'inner'. Neither names a coordinate, so the resolver never has an inner match to prefer and the outer authority key always survives. The sweep therefore proves invariance under NEUTRAL wrapper keys and says nothing whatever about COORDINATE-NAMED ones. This is a sweep that cannot fail on the one shape that matters (freeze 7.2.2).

BLOCKER_B_PD6_01.theAsymmetryThatMakesTHISDirectionLeakAn: Dates are compared unconditionally - `if v5.is_iso_date_value(leaf)` runs regardless of which coordinate the qualifier resolved to. Authorities are compared only under `if coordinate == 'who'`. So the WHEN coordinate is value-shaped and cannot be shadowed away, and the WHO coordinate is key-shaped and can. The forgery half that freeze 4.4 is actually about - a false AUTHORITY - is the half that leaks.
BLOCKER_B_PD6_01.andTheShadowKeyIsDERIVED,NOTALITERAL: Measured: on the live packet, coordinate_keys = {who: {'decidedby'}, when: {'decidedon'}}, so the shadowing key is 'decidedOn'. On a packet renamed to signedOffBy/approvedOn the keys move to {who: {'signedoffby'}, when: {'approvedon'}} - and the escape CLOSES, because 'approvedon' is a member of the inherited FABRICATED_AUTHORITY_KEYS and therefore resolves to WHO first. So the hole exists precisely because the live packet's date key name is one the inherited authority vocabulary does not contain. This makes the finding sharper, not milder: the forger uses the binding packet's own field name as the shadow.

BLOCKER_B_PD6_01.notCoveredByA11: A11 concedes that the SWEEP is a bound and that 'a shape nobody thought of is not swept'. That concession does not license A14's affirmative claim two rows later that 'a forger cannot escape by wrapping', nor the head block's 'handled by construction'. A residual admitting incompleteness and a residual asserting completeness cannot both stand over the same mechanism.
BLOCKER_B_PD6_01.remedy: A successor to THIS file (7.2 forbids editing these bytes). Two independent repairs, either sufficient: (1) coordinate_qualifier returns the SET of coordinates named anywhere on the path rather than the innermost single one, and the leaf is compared under every coordinate it names - which is what 'a leaf is a coordinate if ANY of them qualifies', the file's own stated rule, actually says; or (2) at minimum, prefer WHO over WHEN when both appear on a path, since WHEN is value-shaped and loses nothing by yielding. AND, independently of either: the sweep's wrapper keys must be DERIVED from the live packet's own coordinate key names rather than being the literals 'wrapper' and 'inner', so the sweep can fail on this class. Also: the freeze 4.4 head block's 'CLASS CLOSED ... closed as a CLASS rather than a third instance' should be corrected IN PLACE, appended not rewritten, exactly as this file corrected A7 - because that sentence is in a signature-bound document.

measured.packetSide: Measured separately, and this is the part that matters. With the PACKET's decidedBy set to {}, [], ['sfbreen'], null or 0, packet_attribution collapses to who=[] - and every artifact that then supplies an authority fires ATTRIBUTION-UNRECORDED-AUTHORITY. The packet-side empty container is FAIL-LOUD in the correct direction.

claim4_A12_adjudication.whyTheSTATEDREASONIsWrong: 'There is no scalar to name' is literally true and is the same argument the file explicitly REJECTS for numbers: a number at a coordinate is 'NAMED rather than passed over' precisely because the lane cannot read it. An empty container at a coordinate is a POSITION the lane also cannot read, and the walk holds the full qualifier path at the container node, so the position is nameable with the information already in hand. The distinction drawn is between 'a value I cannot compare' and 'no value at all', and the file's own 7.8.1-rule-1 framing - 'derived from nothing and derived and found nothing must never print the same' - cuts against the concession, not for it.
claim4_A12_adjudication.whyItStillDoesNotEarnABlocker: Threat value is near nil on the artifact side. An empty container ASSERTS NO AUTHORITY. The forgery freeze 4.4 records is an artifact naming a false authority and a false date; `decidedBy: {}` names neither, and is indistinguishable in effect from omitting the field, which is legal by construction under residual A1 (the silent lie is accepted, because the legitimate majority of the corpus cites only state). The dispatch's framing - 'an empty container where an authority belongs is exactly the shape 4.4 is about' - holds for the PACKET, and the packet direction is already fail-loud, as measured above.
claim4_A12_adjudication.recommendation: Keep A12 as a residual. Rewrite its justification from 'there is no scalar to name' to 'an empty container asserts no authority, so it cannot carry the forgery this lane exists to catch; the packet-side case, which could, is fail-loud and measured'. That is a true sentence where the current one is a mechanism excuse.

THE_47TH.title: COORDINATE SHADOWING. coordinate_qualifier resolves a leaf to the INNERMOST coordinate-naming key on its path and discards every outer one, so an object member whose key names the packet's WHEN coordinate strips an authority leaf of its WHO coordinate and neither branch names it. Total silence.
THE_47TH.raisedAsBlockerBecause: Its terminal symptom is identical to blocker B-PD5-01 (zero findings, zero mentions, exit 0), it falsifies three published affirmative sentences including residual A14, and the sweep offered as its proof cannot reach it. See B-PD6-01 above for the full measurement.
THE_47TH.proposedText: the container repair makes NESTING irrelevant to the WALK and leaves it relevant to the RESOLVER. qualified_leaves correctly appends every object key on a leaf's path, but coordinate_qualifier consumes that list by returning on the FIRST match walking inward-out, so a coordinate-naming key nested UNDER an authority-shaped key wins and the authority key is discarded. Because the WHEN branch compares only values that are calendar dates and the type gate names only non-strings, an authority string at {decidedBy: {decidedOn: X}} is neither compared nor named. The shadowing key is the live packet's own date field name and moves with a packet rename; on a packet using approvedOn the escape closes, because approvedOn is in the inherited authority vocabulary and resolves to WHO first. Live incidence measured: 0. NOT REPAIRED HERE.

'by' IS the agent preposition the whole derivation is built on, and it is excluded by an off-by-one. ADJUDICATION_OF_THE_SCOPING_CALL.verdict: UPHELD. 'Not repairable here' is correct on the rule AND on the mechanism, and I found the affirmative evidence the author does not supply.
reasoning: The literal is in check-product-dispositions.py, first-generation reviewed bytes. Freeze 7.2 forbids editing them. Not in dispute.

It is consumed inside v4.validate_v4 -> v2 -> v1, a lane v6 EXECUTES rather than reimplements. v6 cannot reach the comparison without reimplementing the lane, which would retype a reviewed semantic - the thing the whole successor-by-execution design exists to avoid.

THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT, WHICH THE AUTHOR DOES NOT MAKE: the same finding code PD2-1 fires on REMOVAL of an existing decision row (measured: 3 findings) and on a CHANGED decision value (measured: 1 finding). Both are legitimate, substantive detections. So a blanket suppression of PD2-1 - the only suppression available to a caller that does not reimplement the lane - would blind the instrument to a deleted or altered product decision in order to permit an added one. That is a strictly worse trade and it is not a matter of taste.

There is no way to suppress only the additive limb without re-grading a reviewed lane's output. I checked whether v6 re-grades inherited output anywhere else and it does NOT: v4's and v2's findings are extended straight into `failures` untouched. The demotion-to-observation machinery applies only to v6's OWN attribution lane. So the author's line is drawn consistently rather than conveniently.
